current_text.html: A minister of the Gospel against whom there are no charges, if fully satisfied in his own conscience that God has not called him to the ministry, or if he has satisfactory evidence of his inability to serve the Church with acceptance, may report these facts at a stated meeting of Presbytery. At the next stated meeting, if after full deliberation the Presbytery shall concur with him in judgment, it may divest him of his office without censure. This provision shall in like manner apply with any necessary changes to the case of ruling elders and deacons; but in all such cases the Session of the church to which the ruling elder or the deacon who seeks demission belongs shall act as the Presbytery acts in similar cases where a minister is concerned.

relationships.title: Re-examination and divestiture of officers in rotational systems

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that the BCO provides no procedure for re-examining rotated-off officers' qualifications, but divestiture may only occur under BCO 24-6, 38-2, or 34-10.

relationships.title: Session authority over officer nominees and inactive elders under rotation

occurrences.excerpt: A session must present all qualified nominees for election and may not use BCO 24-6 to exclude inactive officers; presbytery proceedings are not automatically required for long-inactive elders.

relationships.title: Teaching elder voting rights and congregational approval of pastoral salary changes

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that a teaching elder votes as a full session member, and that any change to pastoral salary terms requires congregational approval as part of the call.

relationships.title: Myers v. Illiana Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: …is this: I request that Presbytery divest me of my office without censure (BCO 38-2). As I understand it, there are no longer any charges pending against me since judicial process against me was completed with the judgments and censures inflicted on me.…

metadata.synopsis: An elder appealed Presbytery’s elevation, without additional process, of suspensions from office and the Sacraments to deposition and excommunication. The SJC granted the appeal, reversed in whole, and remanded, restoring the prior suspensions. Elevation required a hearing on incorrigibility and contumacy—with a charge, evidence, plea, and defense—but not a full de novo trial; disagreement with the original verdict alone was insufficient. The SJC left unresolved deposition from office when excommunication is absent.

relationships.title: Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: man (BCO 38-2). Thus, any decision that affords ecclesiastical recognition to

metadata.synopsis: Chastain appealed Heritage Presbytery’s 2006 excommunication and deposition. The SJC held the appeal judicially out of order because Chastain had renounced PCA jurisdiction on May 8, 2006. Consequently, Presbytery’s later proceedings were moot and SJC 2005-1 remained in effect. The SJC did not reach the merits. A concurrence questioned the discipline process after renunciation; a dissent argued the majority lacked constitutional authority to recognize unilateral withdrawal and thereby undercut discipline.

relationships.title: Thornton v. Westminster Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: voluntarily demitting his office (BCO 38-2). A presbytery removes its

metadata.synopsis: Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s refusal to place Memorial PCA Session’s call in his hands and its simultaneous initiation of administrative divestiture without censure. The SJC sustained both issues, reversed the divestiture decision, and remanded with directions to approve and deliver the call and set an installation date. A valid call supplied the congregational approbation whose absence BCO 34-10’s administrative remedy requires; Presbytery also could not rely on undisclosed concerns while avoiding required judicial process. The ruling found clear error, not an absence of all presbyterial review authority.

relationships.title: Anthony Dallison v. North Florida Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: …divest him from the office of Teaching Elder, according to the provisions of BCO 38-2. In response to this request, Presbytery appointed a committee to determine compliance of TE Dallison with the terms of the May 27, 1997 censure (#3 above).

…15, 2000 Dallison requested the privilege to demit the ministry according to BCO 38-2 which necessarily required that court to lift their censure against him. That request was tantamount to an admission by the Complainant that presbytery has the power to…

metadata.synopsis: After TE Anthony Dallison confessed spousal abuse and received an indefinite suspension, North Florida Presbytery later found him impenitent and deposed him and suspended him from the sacraments. Dallison complained that increasing the censure required fresh charges and trial. The SJC disagreed: his BCO 38-1 confession waived trial rights as to the original charge; the offender then had to satisfy the court of repentance, and the presbytery could investigate and impose higher censure under BCO 37-3, 37-4, 37-8, and 34-4b. The complaint was not sustained.
